mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved sequentially from -39.1% (t-2w) to -28.3% (t-0w), a 10.8 percentage point recovery over two weeks. This sustained upward trend in retail mobility signals restoration of consumer confidence and foot traffic patterns that will persist into the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further above the recent baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 10.8 points over t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below the mean of the last 28 days, or declines week-on-week in 3 of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has recovered from -28.7% (t-2w) to -16.7% (t-0w), a 12-point improvement. Increased transit use indicates commuting resumption and urban circulation, which directly enables retail and recreation visits. This transit recovery will drive RETAIL_REC gains over the next week as commuters access retail zones.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 12 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility declines in the next week, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve in week t+1w relative to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has converged to near-baseline (0.3% at t-0w) from -16.1% at t-3w, indicating essential-goods shopping has normalized. When essential mobility stabilizes, discretionary retail and recreation spending increases as households redirect mobility budget to non-essential venues. This substitution effect will elevate RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -5% and remains stable
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 0.3% vs -16.1% three weeks prior
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM declines below -5% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its t-0w level in the mean of weeks t+1w through t+4w.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains severely depressed at -28.7% (t-0w), showing no recovery trend. Persistent park closures or restrictions signal ongoing containment measures that constrain all outdoor mobility, including retail and recreation. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed and fail to improve significantly over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -25% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -28.7% with no improvement from t-2w (-36.9%)
failure_condition: PARKS mobility improves by more than 10 points in any single week, or RETAIL_REC exceeds -20% in the mean of weeks t+1w through t+4w.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stabilized at 5-7% elevation across all four weeks, indicating sustained work-from-home adoption and reduced commuting. When residential occupancy remains elevated, retail and recreation mobility is suppressed because consumers remain home-based. This persistent residential elevation will constrain RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 5% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL elevated at 5.1-9.3% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below 2% in any week, or RETAIL_REC improves by more than 15 points in the mean of weeks t+1w through t+4w relative to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized at -23% to -31% with no recovery trend, while RETAIL_REC has improved 10.8 points. This decoupling indicates retail recovery is driven by discretionary weekend/leisure mobility rather than commute-linked weekday retail. If WORKPLACES remains suppressed while RETAIL_REC continues recovering, the mechanism is leisure-driven substitution that will sustain RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -20% AND RETAIL_REC improves week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES flat at -23% to -31% while RETAIL_REC improved 10.8 points
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and RETAIL_REC both decline in the same week, or RETAIL_REC mean over t+1w to t+4w falls below t-0w level.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has recovered 12 points (from -28.7% to -16.7%) while WORKPLACES remains flat at -23.6%. This indicates transit recovery is driven by non-commute trips (shopping, leisure, errands). When transit serves discretionary mobility, RETAIL_REC gains are amplified. Over the next two weeks, this transit-retail coupling will drive accelerated RETAIL_REC improvement.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves more than 5 points while WORKPLACES remains flat or declines
failure_condition: TRANSIT declines in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve in both weeks t+1w and t+2w relative to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM normalization (0.3% at t-0w) combined with PARKS remaining severely depressed (-28.7%) indicates a regime where essential mobility has recovered but outdoor leisure remains restricted. Under this asymmetric constraint, consumers will shift discretionary spending to indoor retail venues as a substitute for unavailable parks. This substitution will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
